questions.cardText:
[Zoology] What animals do farmer ants domesticate?
A. Aphids B. Beetles C. Earthworms
Answer: A. Farmer ants herd aphids to the juiciest parts of plants to feed, protect them from predators, and even carry them into their nests at night. In return, the ants “milk” the aphids by stroking them with their antennae to harvest the sweet honeydew they secrete. Sometimes, the ants even transport aphid eggs to new locations to maintain their herds.
questions.de: Welche Insekten hüten Ameisen wie Vieh, schützen sie vor Fressfeinden und „melken“ sie mit ihren Fühlern, um süßen Honigtau zu gewinnen?
questions.en: Which insects do farming ants herd, protect from predators and “milk” with their antennae for sweet honeydew?

timeline.labelEn: Pierre André Latreille formally names the aphid superfamily Aphidoidea
timeline.labelDe: Pierre André Latreille benennt die Überfamilie der Blattläuse (Aphidoidea) wissenschaftlich

questions.notes: Card's answer confirmed (farming ants protect aphid herds, store their eggs over winter and carry hatchlings to plants).

questions.cardText:
[Archaeology] What was the first city to reach a population of one million?
A. Rome B. Beijing C. Cairo
Answer: A. Rome was the first city to reach a population of one million people around 133 BCE.
questions.de: Welche antike Stadt gilt meist als erste Stadt der Welt mit rund einer Million Einwohnern?
questions.en: Which ancient city is usually named as the first in the world to reach a population of about one million?

timeline.labelEn: Ancient Rome is estimated to have about one million inhabitants around the start of the Common Era
timeline.labelDe: Das antike Rom hat Schätzungen zufolge um den Beginn unserer Zeitrechnung rund eine Million Einwohner

source.title: List of largest cities throughout history

questions.notes: Card's answer (Rome) is the usual claim but its date is doubtful: Wikipedia's list puts Rome at about 1,000,000 around AD 1 and says Rome, Jiankang and Chang'an may have been the first to reach a million, as early as the 1st century AD; no fetched source supports 'around 133 BCE'. Estimates for Rome range widely (450,000 to about one million).
